description:
Run Renovate in dry-run mode to preview what it would do — no PRs opened, no git pushes. Returns a structured JSON report plus a top-level `ok` boolean (false when the CLI failed OR the report records a validation/error-level problem, even if the exit code was 0). RE2 native-module fallback noise and Renovate's `Unsupported node environment` notice are filtered out of `reportErrors` — the former flows into `warnings` (still actionable, still surfaced), the latter into a separate `environmentWarnings[]` since the run still produced a usable report.

Effective platform = `platform` input → `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` env → `local`. The `platformSource` field on the result echoes which step won; preflight errors and the env-overrides-default advisory both reference it so callers don't have to read the source to find where a surprising `gitlab`/`github` came from.

The full structured report ships inline by default. For large repos that is bigger than most MCP clients' response-content cap (≈75 KB on Claude Desktop) and the middle of the JSON is silently truncated. Pass `reportOutputPath` to redirect the structured report to a file (mode 0600), in which case `summary.report` collapses to `{ reportPath, repoCount, updateCount }` and `dry_run_diff` can pick it up via `{ reportPath: … }`. `warnings`, `problems`, `reportErrors`, and `environmentWarnings` always stay inline regardless — those are the actionable bits.

**Custom base branches.** By default Renovate evaluates the repository's default branch. Pass `baseBranches` to evaluate other branches instead — this is how you dry-run a Renovate config change that lives on a feature branch before merging it. Entries are exact branch names; regex requires `/…/` wrapping (e.g. `/^renovate\/.+/`, negate with `!/…/`) — bare `^foo` is matched literally, not as regex. `$default` expands to the default branch. With `readConfigFromBaseBranch` (default true) Renovate also reads its config FROM those branches (`useBaseBranchConfig=merge`), so the branch's edited config is what gets evaluated; set it false to scan the branches' manifests using the default branch's config. Base-branch selection only applies to remote-platform runs (`platform: 'github'`/`'gitlab'`) — it is ignored (with a warning) under `platform=local`.

**Auth — prefer env vars, every token bound to its host.** Set tokens on the MCP server's env via `claude_desktop_config.json` / `.mcp.json`, with the same host scoping `resolve_config` uses: `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` (and the Gitea / Forgejo / Bitbucket ones) only for their platform's public host, `RENOVATE_TOKEN` only for the home host named by `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` / `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` (where it wins over the platform's own token, as in Renovate), `RENOVATE_MCP_HOST_TOKENS` entries for further hosts. The `platform`, `endpoint` and `presetPlatform` inputs and the repo's origin route requests but never bind an env token to another host: an endpoint passed only on the call gets a token from a `RENOVATE_MCP_HOST_TOKENS` entry or the `token` input. On a remote run (`github` / `gitlab`) the platform token — the `token` input, else the env token bound to the API host (`endpoint`, else `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` when it belongs to that platform, else the public API) — is exported as `RENOVATE_TOKEN` to the spawned Renovate CLI; without one an actionable error is returned before spawning. Under `platform=local` no `RENOVATE_TOKEN` is exported and the `token` input is ignored with a warning. Every env token is also handed to Renovate as a host rule on its own host (`GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` excepted, Renovate reads it itself), so a `GITLAB_TOKEN` authenticates gitlab.com lookups in a local run. A malformed `RENOVATE_MCP_HOST_TOKENS` is an error before spawning. The `token` input is retained as an ad-hoc / testing fallback — when supplied inline it is persisted in the MCP tool transcript that the client may share, replay, or feed back into the LLM, so an advisory entry is appended to the result `warnings` array steering callers toward env-var auth.

Default mode runs `--platform=local` against the filesystem at `repoPath`. Renovate cannot resolve `local>…` presets (or unprefixed `owner/repo` ones) in local mode, so the tool flattens them first, in every `dryRunMode` (Renovate resolves presets during repo init in all of them): it copies the repository (tracked files only: an untracked or gitignored file Renovate would read from disk, such as a local `.npmrc`, is not in the copy) into a temporary directory, resolves every preset after the leading built-ins with Renovate's own preset resolver, routed through `presetPlatform` (else the platform of the origin remote) and `endpoint` (else `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` when `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` names the same platform and, for an origin-derived platform, the endpoint is on the origin's host), validates the result as a repo config, writes it into the copy and runs Renovate there. The copy's path is reported as `repoPath` and the copy is removed afterwards; the result lists `flattenedPresets` and `keptExtends`. Refused before spawning: no derivable route (pass `presetPlatform`, or set `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` / `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` for the origin's host), a self-hosted origin without an endpoint, Bitbucket, a blocked endpoint, a preset that cannot be fetched, a flattened config that fails validation, a worker failure, a config file with local presets that git does not track, or a repository over the copy caps. An `extract` run without a derivable route is not refused: it runs unflattened with a warning, and Renovate reports the preset itself. Alternatively pass `platform` (`github` or `gitlab`), `endpoint` and `repository` (plus `token` when no env token applies) to run as a real platform client against the remote repository — Renovate still runs with `--dry-run`, so no PRs are opened. `gitlab>…` / `github>…` presets always come from gitlab.com / github.com, as in Renovate.

Credentials for private registries (e.g. `COMPOSER_AUTH` for Packagist/Satis proxies, `NPM_TOKEN` / `.npmrc` for npm, Docker registry creds, `RENOVATE_HOST_RULES` for anything else) must be set on the MCP server process itself — via the `env` key in `claude_desktop_config.json` / `.mcp.json`, not your shell, since the MCP server runs as a child of Claude and does not inherit shell env. Alternatively, encode credentials as `hostRules` in the Renovate config, or pass them per-call via the `hostRules` input on this tool (written after the env-token rules to a mode-0600 temp file that is cleaned up after the run; token/password values — including the platform `token` input, the env tokens and `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` — are scrubbed from `logTail`, `problems` and the report, `reportErrors` and a saved `reportOutputPath` included). A per-call rule carrying a credential replaces the env-token rule for the same host (an env rule that would outrank it in Renovate's host-rule lookup is left out), with or without a `hostType`. Per-call `hostRules` are appended to any the repo's own config already declares. If a lookup can't auth to a registry, Renovate often reports 0 updates without a loud error; when that happens this tool surfaces detected auth failures under `problems` in the output so callers can distinguish a genuine "no updates" from a silent registry-auth failure.

baseBranches.description: One or more base branches to evaluate instead of the repository's default branch (Renovate's `baseBranchPatterns`). Each entry is an EXACT branch name unless it is wrapped in slashes: only `/…/`-delimited entries are treated as regex (optionally `!/…/` to negate) — a bare `^release/.*` is matched literally as a branch named `^release/.*` and will never match. The magic value `$default` expands to the repository's default branch. This is what lets you dry-run a Renovate config change that lives on a non-default branch (e.g. a feature branch) before it is merged. Maps to the `RENOVATE_BASE_BRANCH_PATTERNS` env var — `baseBranchPatterns` is not a CLI flag. Only applies to remote-platform runs (`platform: 'github'`/`'gitlab'`); ignored under `platform=local`, which always inspects the working tree at `repoPath`. See also `readConfigFromBaseBranch`.

configContent.description: Local runs only: a draft Renovate config to run instead of the repo's own, without writing it. dry_run copies the repository into a temporary directory (the same copy and caps as local-preset flattening), writes the draft there over the config file Renovate would read (a new `renovate.json` when there is none; under `package.json#renovate` the other keys are kept), runs Renovate in the copy and removes it; `repoPath` is never written. Local presets in the draft are flattened as usual. Validation is Renovate's own: config errors surface in `reportErrors`. Refused with `platform: github` / `gitlab`, whose runs read the config from the platform. The result's `configSource` says which config ran (`input` or `repo`).

dryRunMode.description: extract = detect manifests only; lookup = resolve latest versions; full = full simulation including branches/PRs (default)

endpoint.description: Custom API base URL (e.g. `https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/` or `https://ghe.example.com/api/v3/`) for a remote run (`platform=github`/`gitlab`), forwarded as `--endpoint`; falls back to `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` from the server env when `platform` is unset or equals `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` (otherwise the env endpoint is kept from the child). It routes requests only: an env token reaches its host only when `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` / `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` name that host or a `RENOVATE_MCP_HOST_TOKENS` entry covers it. Under `platform=local` it routes the local presets the tool flattens (with `presetPlatform`), and is ignored with a warning when nothing is flattened. `gitlab>…` / `github>…` presets always go to gitlab.com / github.com.

hostRules.description: Optional per-invocation Renovate hostRules for private registry auth. Written after the env-token host rules to a mode-0600 temp file that is passed via the RENOVATE_CONFIG_FILE env var (RENOVATE_ADDITIONAL_CONFIG_FILE when the operator already set RENOVATE_CONFIG_FILE; refused when both are set) and deleted after the run. Token/password values are scrubbed from any log output this tool returns. Appended to (not replacing) any hostRules declared in the repo's own config.

items.description: A single Renovate hostRule (matchHost, hostType, username, password, token, …). Structure is not validated here — Renovate's own config loader checks it when the temp file is read.

platform.description: Renovate platform to run as. When unset, falls back to `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` from the MCP server's env (if it's one of `local`/`github`/`gitlab`), then to `local`. Default `local` runs against the filesystem at `repoPath`. Set `github` or `gitlab` (with `endpoint` + `token` + `repository`) to run a full remote dry-run — this is what you need when your config extends `local>` presets that live on a private GitHub Enterprise / self-hosted GitLab. Still no PRs opened because `--dry-run` is always set.

presetPlatform.description: Local runs only: the platform the config's local presets (`local>owner/repo`, or an unprefixed `owner/repo`) live on. Under `platform=local` Renovate cannot resolve them, so dry_run resolves them first with Renovate's own preset resolver, writes the result into a temporary copy of the repository and runs Renovate there. When unset, it is derived from the origin remote (github.com, gitlab.com, gitea.com, codeberg.org, code.forgejo.org, or the flavour of a self-hosted host, which then needs `endpoint` or `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT`; a host whose flavour the name does not show is taken as `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` when `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` is on it). Passing it also flattens a config whose local presets only appear inside other presets. `bitbucket` is refused: Renovate reads Bitbucket local presets through its platform client. Like `platform` in `resolve_config` it routes the presets but never moves an env token to their host.

readConfigFromBaseBranch.description: Only meaningful together with `baseBranches`. When true (default), Renovate reads its config (renovate.json/.jsonc/.json5, …) FROM each base branch — `useBaseBranchConfig=merge` — so a config edit that only exists on that branch is actually evaluated. Set false to scan the base branches' manifests while still using the default branch's config.

repoPath.description: Absolute path to the repository root. Required for the default `platform=local` mode. When `platform` is overridden (e.g. `gitlab` / `github`), Renovate runs against the remote `repository` instead — `repoPath` is still used as the child's working directory but its manifest files are ignored.

reportOutputPath.description: Optional absolute path to copy the structured Renovate report to (created fresh with mode 0600 — the path must not already exist, or the call fails with `already exists` rather than overwriting). When set, `summary.report` is replaced by `{ reportPath, repoCount, updateCount }` so the inline response stays under MCP response-content caps. Use this — together with `dry_run_diff`'s `{ reportPath }` input — when the full inline report would exceed the harness truncation threshold (≈75 KB on Claude Desktop). `warnings`/`problems`/`reportErrors`/`environmentWarnings` always stay inline regardless.

repository.description: Identifier of the repository Renovate should operate on, passed as a positional argument (Renovate has no `--repository` flag). For GitHub: `owner/repo`. For GitLab: `group/project` or a nested-group path like `group/subgroup/project` — both are accepted. Required when `platform` is `github`/`gitlab`. Ignored when `platform=local`.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait time in ms (default 5 minutes, capped at 15)

token.description: Platform token for a remote run (`platform=github`/`gitlab`), exported as `RENOVATE_TOKEN` to the child. Scrubbed from any log output this tool returns. When omitted, the env token bound to the API host is used: `RENOVATE_TOKEN` (then `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN`) on the `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` / `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` host, `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` on the public host, or a `RENOVATE_MCP_HOST_TOKENS` entry for that host — same host scoping as `resolve_config`. Ignored with a warning under `platform=local`, where there is no platform host to send it to.
